subject: APAC1: planned capacity reshuffle & hotpatch window (Mar 21)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: infra-eng@cumulusai.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: APAC1: planned capacity reshuffle & hotpatch window (Mar 21)

Hi Ashley and Cumulus infra team,

Heads-up: we have a planned capacity reshuffle + critical hotpatch for APAC1 scheduled for Tue, 21 Mar 2028 between 02:00-05:00 UTC. The work is a two-stage operation: first we will rebalance active inference capacity across racks to remove hotspots, then apply a short kernel hotpatch that fixes a NIC race observed under very specific backplane conditions.

Expected user impact:
- Typical inference requests: no interruption for most customers.
- A small subset of requests may see a brief endpoint eviction (up to ~90s) during live handover when a node is drained.
- Persistent KV caches will be retained on a best-effort basis; we will avoid full model reloads where possible.

What we will do on our side:
- Live-drain nodes in a staged cadence (1 rack at a time) with automatic traffic failover to healthy nodes.
- Automatic fallback to compatible model variant (if configured).
- Extra monitoring and rollback gates; an on-call engineer will be dedicated to rollback decisioning.

Action items for customers:
- No mandatory action required. If you run long-running batch jobs or heavy cold-start traffic during the window, please consider delaying them or enabling client-side retry with exponential backoff.
- If you rely on an in-memory prefix cache for low-latency inference, reply here and we will coordinate a short test window before the main event.

Attachments: apac1-capacity-reshuffle-diagram.png, apac1-hotpatch-runbook-v1.pdf
Runbook/Status links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/APAC1-reshuffle-20280321

We’ll post rolling updates to the status page and ping here if any change to timing is required.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

From: infra-eng@cumulusai.com <infra-eng@cumulusai.com>

Subject: Re: APAC1: planned capacity reshuffle & hotpatch window (Mar 21)

Thanks for the heads-up, Soojin — appreciate the detail. Two quick clarifications:

1) KV cache persistence: if a node is live-drained and the KV cache is best-effort, should we expect a model reload (cold-start penalty) for requests routed to the replacement node?
2) Client-side retries: do you have a recommended retry budget (count + base delay) you’ve observed to minimize duplicate completions for typical text-gen calls?

Ashley Kim
Infra Engineering Lead, Cumulus AI
ashley.kim@cumulusai.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: infra-eng@cumulusai.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 03:10:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: APAC1: planned capacity reshuffle & hotpatch window (Mar 21)

Hi Ashley — quick answers: 

On KV cache persistence: we will preserve KV caches for warm handovers where the replacement node has a compatible cache snapshot; however, in ~5-10% of handovers the cache will be dropped and a model cold-start may occur. We’ve tuned the hotpatch to avoid full IR unloads, so typical cold-start penalty is ~1.5-2x latency for the first few tokens, not a full model reload.

On retries: we recommend a conservative client retry budget of up to 2 retries with an initial backoff of 250ms and exponential growth (250ms, 500ms) for typical short-generation calls. For long-running streaming sessions, prefer server-side reconnect semantics rather than full-request retries.

We’ll run a short smoke test with one partner the week of Mar 18 to validate cache behavior — happy to add Cumulus if you want early visibility. If you prefer a deeper technical sync, Monica and I can hop on a call; otherwise we’ll publish a brief post-event notes summary on the status page.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
